pages.title: What you will learn
pages.body:
> 🔤 **Strand 2 — Algebra**
Using letters and symbols to describe patterns, relationships and unknown quantities.

> 🎯 **Content standard** (B9.2.2)
- B9.2.2.1 — Demonstrate understanding of (i) change of subject, (ii) substituting values to evaluate expressions, and (iii) factorising expressions that have a simple binomial as a factor.

> 🎯 **In this chapter you will learn to:**
- change the subject of a formula
- substitute values into formulae to evaluate them and solve problems
- factorise expressions by taking out common factors
- use simplifying and factorising to solve real-world problems

lessons.title: Changing the subject of a formula

pages.title: Changing the subject of a formula
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Perform change of subject of a given formula and use it to solve problems.
Curriculum indicator B9.2.2.1.1
> 🔑 **Key idea: Subject of a formula** — In A = lw, **A** is the **subject** — it stands alone on one side. To make another letter the subject, use inverse operations on both sides (as when solving an equation) until that letter stands alone.
## ✏️ Example 6.1
Make x the subject of each formula: a) y = x + c b) y = mx + c c) P = 2(x + w) d) A = [[1/2]]xh e) [[x/a]] − b = c f) y = sqrt{x + k}
**Solution**
a) **x = y − c**
b) y − c = mx ⟹ **x =** [[y − c/m]]
c) [[P/2]] = x + w ⟹ **x =** [[P/2]] **− w**
d) 2A = xh ⟹ **x =** [[2A/h]]
e) [[x/a]] = b + c ⟹ **x = a(b + c)**
f) Square both sides: y² = x + k ⟹ **x = y² − k**
## ✏️ Example 6.2
Use change of subject to solve each problem.
a) The area of a rectangle is 24 cm². If the length is 8 cm, find the width.
b) The area of a circle is A = πr². If A = 154 cm², find r (π = [[22/7]]).
c) A triangle has area 54 cm² and base 12 cm. Find its height.
d) A cylinder has volume 330 cm³ and radius 3.5 cm. Find its height (V = πr²h, π = [[22/7]]).
**Solution**
a) A = lw ⟹ w = [[A/l]] = [[24/8]] = **3 cm**
b) r² = [[A/π]] = 154 × [[7/22]] = 49 ⟹ **r = 7 cm**
c) A = [[1/2]]bh ⟹ h = [[2A/b]] = [[108/12]] = **9 cm**
d) h = [[V/πr^{2}]] = 330/((22/7)×12.25) = [[330/38.5]] ≈ **8.57 cm**

pages.title: Substituting into formulae
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Substitute values into given formulae to evaluate them and use them to solve problems.
Curriculum indicator B9.2.2.1.2
## ✏️ Example 6.3
a) Find the value of (x − b)² − 3(x − b) if x = 2 and b = −5. b) Make k the subject of [[1/n]] = sqrt{[[k^{2} + a^{2}/hg]]}, and find k when n = [[1/2]], a = 3, h = 2 and g = 32. c) The volume of a cone is V = [[1/3]]πr²h. Find V when r = 7, h = 21 and π = [[22/7]].
**Solution**
a) x − b = 2 − (−5) = 7. So 7² − 3(7) = 49 − 21 = **28**
b) Square: [[1/n^{2}]] = [[k^{2} + a^{2}/hg]] ⟹ k² = [[hg/n^{2}]] − a² ⟹ **k =** sqrt{[[hg/n^{2}]] − a^{2}}
When n = [[1/2]], n² = [[1/4]]: k = sqrt{(2 × 32)/(1/4) − 9} = sqrt{256 − 9} = sqrt{247} ≈ **15.72**
c) V = [[1/3]] × [[22/7]] × 49 × 21 = **1,078 cubic units**

pages.title: Factorising expressions
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Factorise expressions that have a simple binomial.
Curriculum indicator B9.2.2.1.3
> 🔑 **Key idea: Factorising with a common factor** — Find the **HCF** of all the terms (numbers and letters), write it outside a bracket, and divide each term by it to get the terms inside. Always check by expanding.
## ✏️ Example 6.4
Factorise: a) 3x + 4xy b) 12ab + 16b c) −13xy + 39x d) 5y − 2y² + 3y e) 8y − 2y² f) −6x + 12
**Solution**
a) **x(3 + 4y)**
b) **4b(3a + 4)**
c) **−13x(y − 3)** (or 13x(3 − y))
d) First collect like terms: 8y − 2y² = **2y(4 − y)**
e) **2y(4 − y)**
f) **−6(x − 2)** (or 6(2 − x), or −3(2x − 4) — but −6(x − 2) is fully factorised because 6 is the HCF)
> ⚠️ **Watch out!** Factorise **completely**: take out the **highest** common factor. 12ab + 16b = 2b(6a + 8) is correct but not complete, because 6a + 8 still has a common factor 2.

pages.title: Solving real-world problems
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Use the knowledge of simplifying and factorising expressions to solve real-world problems.
Curriculum indicator B9.2.2.1.4
## ✏️ Example 6.5
You buy 10 items at a shopping plaza. Each plastic bag holds only 3 items. How many bags do you need?
**Solution**
Let x = number of items = 10 and y = capacity of one bag = 3.
Bags needed = [[x/y]] = [[10/3]] = 3.33…
You cannot use part of a bag, so round **up**: you need **4 bags**.
## ✏️ Example 6.6
Two dozen eggs cost GH₵10, a loaf of bread costs GH₵5 and a bottle of juice costs GH₵8. How much money is needed for two dozen eggs, three loaves and five bottles of juice?
**Solution**
Let a = 10, b = 5, c = 8. Money needed = a + 3b + 5c = 10 + 15 + 40 = **GH₵65**
## ✏️ Example 6.7
The area of a rectangle is 72 cm². The length is twice the width. Find the length and the width.
**Solution**
Let the width be x; then the length is 2x.
x × 2x = 72 ⟹ 2x² = 72 ⟹ x² = 36 ⟹ x = 6 (a length cannot be negative)
Width = **6 cm**, length = **12 cm**.
## ✏️ Example 6.8
A field is made of two rectangles of widths 7.5 m and 12.5 m, each 28 m long. Use factorisation to find the total area quickly.
**Solution**
Area = 28 × 7.5 + 28 × 12.5 = 28(7.5 + 12.5) = 28 × 20 = **560 m²**

pages.body:

pages.title: Chapter 6 summary
pages.body:
- To change the subject, undo operations in reverse order on both sides.
- Substitute carefully, using brackets for negatives.
- Factorise by taking out the HCF; check by expanding.
